newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-EMAP in talks on business titles.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-EMAP in talks on business titles.

text.p: EMAP Plc said on Monday it had received an approach from a potential buyer of a number of its business magazines including "UK Press Gazette" and "Media Week".
"One party expressed an interest in those two plus some others," chief executive Robin Miller told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"We do confirm that some discussions have taken place," he added.
Miller said EMAP constantly looked at its own portfolio to see which titles were the best fit for the future. He said the company had around 60 regular business magazine titles.
The chief executive refused to be drawn on speculation regarding the successor to chairman Sir John Hoskyns, who will retire in July 1998.
"We have 13 months and matters will be discussed during that time," he said.
Miller is seen as a likely candidate for the chairmanship, leaving a vacancy for the post of chief executive.

EMAP had a choppy year in the boardroom, losing two rebel non-executive directors last December after a row over corporate governance. That was followed by the departure in April of long-serving managing director David Arculus, who defected to United News & Media.
EMAP has not recruited a specific replacement for Arculus but instead parcelled up his responsibilities among a range of senior management.

Miller said underlying revenues were flat in France as difficult economic conditions persisted there. But he said there were indications of an improvement in advertising in the second half and some signs of this carrying over into the early part of the current year.
EMAP booked a one-off gain of 113.5 million stg from the sale of its regional newspaper business a year ago
Its net debt fell to 89 million stg from 350 million.
The company said there was scope for further investment in new product launches and acquisitions.
